"""Diacritic removal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unicodedata


def strip_accents(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove diacritical marks (accents) from ``text``.

    ``"café"`` becomes ``"cafe"``. Characters that carry no diacritic are
    returned unchanged.

    Args:
        text: Input text.

    Returns:
        ``text`` without diacritical marks.
    """
    # Decompose precomposed accented letters into a base letter plus
    # combining marks, drop the combining marks, then re-normalize to NFC
    # so that characters without diacritics (CJK, Hangul syllables,
    # ligatures, ``ß``, ...) come back with their original code points.
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text)
    stripped = "".join(ch for ch in decomposed if unicodedata.category(ch) != "Mn")
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFC", stripped)

arguments.command:
python - <<'EOF'
from textkit.accents import strip_accents

cases = {
    "café": "cafe",
    "日本語": "日本語",
    "naïve": "naive",
    "Ångström": "Angstrom",
    "e\u0301": "e",                     # separate combining accent
    "Å\u030a": "A",                    # combining ring above (Å = A + ring)
    "cafe\u0301\u0302": "cafe",        # multiple combining marks
    "plain ASCII 123!": "plain ASCII 123!",
    "": "",
    "ß": "ß",                          # no decomposition
    "日本語です": "日本語です",
    "한국어": "한국어",
    "fi\u0302": "fi\u0302",            # tilde stays (it is Mn? no, tilde is Sk) -> unchanged
    "café\n\t": "cafe\n\t",
    "café\u0301": "cafe",             # decomposed accent removed
}
for inp, exp in cases.items():
    got = strip_accents(inp)
    status = "OK " if got == exp else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status} {repr(inp)} -> {repr(got)} (expected {repr(exp)})")

# code-point exactness for non-accented text
for s in ["日本語", "한국어", "fi\u0302", "ß"]:
    assert strip_accents(s) == s, f"{s!r} changed to {strip_accents(s)!r}"
# combining diacritic category check
print("category of \\u0301:", unicodedata.category("\u0301") if False else "Mn")
EOF

    "Ångström": "Angstrom",
